answer_raw:
The best option depends on your personal style, but a **full shave** is the most efficient for maintenance and hides patchy hair better than any other option [4].

**The Full Shave**
A razor shave is the ideal choice if you have bald spots or patchy hair, as it looks better than losing hair patch by patch [4]. To maintain a smooth look, you should shave daily or up to every three days at most if using a foil razor [6]. For a close, shiny bald head, a tool like the **Skull Shaver Pitbull** works well, provided your hair is short enough [6].

**The Buzz Cut**
A buzz cut or a "high and tight" military-inspired cut is functional, masculine, and helps hide the signs of balding [4]. This is a lower-maintenance alternative to a full shave, though you'll still need regular clipper passes to keep the length uniform [4].

**Keeping the Sides**
If you have dense hair on the sides but thinning on top, a **skin fade** creates a cleaner transition and makes the haircut look intentional [1]. Shorter sides can also make your overall hairstyle look neater, giving you more license to style the remaining hair on top [3]. 

**Comparison of Maintenance and Aesthetics**

| Option | Maintenance Level | Aesthetic Impact |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Full Shave** | **Highest** (requires frequent shaving) | Hides patches and provides a clean, intentional look [4]. |
| **Buzz Cut** | **Low** (requires regular clipper trims) | Masculine and hides balding signs through uniformity [4]. |
| **Keep Sides** | **Moderate** (requires regular tapering/fades) | Uses side density to balance top thinning [1][3]. |
